samples.scenario: An enterprise ransomware infection where threat actors use a multi-stage attack: initial access via phishing, lateral movement with stolen credentials, exfiltration of sensitive documents using a custom encrypted tunnel over TCP port 8443, followed by mass encryption of endpoint files and deployment of ransom notes demanding payment in cryptocurrency.

samples.detection_method: Endpoint detection identifies suspicious PowerShell commands downloading executables from unknown domains. Network monitoring detects encrypted tunnels over non-standard port 8443 to external IPs. File integrity monitoring alerts on bulk creation of .encrypted files and ransom note text files. Registry monitoring logs new persistence keys under current user run keys. Correlation between these events triggers ransomware detection workflow focused on data exfiltration and encryption.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1560.002 - Archive via Archive via Encrypted Channel

samples.detection_method: Scheduled task monitoring detects new or modified tasks executing PowerShell scripts with bypassed execution policies. Network monitoring identifies FTP connections transferring large encrypted backup files to suspicious external IPs. File integrity monitoring raises alerts on mass encryption of backup archives and ransom note deployments. Registry monitoring tracks suspicious scheduled task creation or modification. Correlation of these events supports detection of ransomware with exfiltration on backup servers.
